mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 600K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 600K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 8%, indicating a strong labor market, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the combined effect boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and stock performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month, signaling reduced supply chain pressures, leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as input costs decrease.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate, as a broad indicator of economic activity, positively correlates with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, reflecting the overall health of the economy.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP and stock market correlation
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns do not significantly correlate with GDP growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 2%, and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth rate exceeds 3% in a quarter, the combined inflationary pressure and monetary tightening predict negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL growth > 3% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Threshold-triggered: an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 1% in two months signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market shocks and stock reactions
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE increases > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: Regime-conditional: in a post-shock recovery regime, a resurgence in retail sales (RSAFS) above $400B, indicating strong consumer demand, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, outperforming the baseline.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when RSAFS > $400B in post-shock recovery, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.
